verdict.rationale: Glama's own browser-based MCP Inspector connects to any MCP server, including local ones exposed through mcp-proxy, and exercises its tools, resources and prompts. That is a first-party MCP-client capability. However, there is no evidence that Glama's AI product (Glama Chat) lets a model plug in MCP servers and call their tools during conversations; the gateway and hosting features proxy other agents' calls rather than letting Glama use the tools itself. Missing for 10: documented MCP-client support in Glama Chat for model-driven tool use, configuration docs for adding servers to the chat assistant, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
Search, compare, and connect to thousands of MCP servers
